questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 52-year-old woman on treatment for breast cancer presented with headaches and vomiting. CSF cytology showed malignant cells. MRI revealed leptomeningeal enhancement suggestive of metastases. Which of the following meningeal layers are affected?

options.text: Dura mater, arachnoid mater, and pia mater

questions.explanation: Leptomeninges are the arachnoid mater and pia mater. The dura mater is the pachymeninx. The source also notes that meningeal enhancement may occur in meningitis, encephalitis, tumors/metastases, inflammatory vasculitis and after seizures, trauma or surgery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about meninges is false?

options.text: Endosteal layer of the dura mater is the periosteum of skull bones
Meningeal layer divides the cranial cavity into freely communicating spaces
Dural venous sinuses are present between the endosteal and the meningeal layer
Both endosteal and meningeal layer contain fibroblasts and osteoblasts

questions.correctAnswerText: Both endosteal and meningeal layer contain fibroblasts and osteoblasts
questions.explanation: Both endosteal and meningeal dural layers contain fibroblasts, but only the endosteal layer contains osteoblasts. Dural venous sinuses lie between the two layers. The meningeal layer forms the dural partitions: falx cerebri, tentorium cerebelli, falx cerebelli and diaphragma sellae.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Both endosteal and meningeal dural layers contain fibroblasts, but only the endosteal layer contains osteoblasts. Dural venous sinuses lie between the two layers. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 42-year-old lady presented with sudden onset severe headache, aphasia, and diplopia. Imaging shows an empty delta sign of superior sagittal sinus thrombosis. Choose the correct statement about the dural fold containing the affected sinus.

options.text: It separates the cerebellum from the occipital lobes of the cerebrum.
It separates the two cerebellar hemispheres.

questions.explanation: The superior sagittal sinus lies in the falx cerebri. Falx cerebri separates the two cerebral hemispheres; its upper fixed margin contains the superior sagittal sinus, its lower free margin the inferior sagittal sinus, and its attachment to tentorium cerebelli contains the straight sinus. Tentorium separates cerebellum from occipital lobes; falx cerebelli separates cerebellar hemispheres and contains the occipital sinus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nerves do not innervate the marked structure?
questions.explanation: The marked structure is cranial dura mater. It is innervated mainly by the three divisions of the trigeminal nerve, C2-C3 spinal nerves and cervical sympathetic fibers. Facial nerve branches do not innervate it.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The marked structure is cranial dura mater. It is innervated mainly by the three divisions of the trigeminal nerve, C2-C3 spinal nerves and cervical sympathetic fibers. Facial nerve branches do not innervate it.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which part of the dura mater is supplied by all the three branches of the trigeminal nerve?

options.text: Dura of the anterior cranial fossa
Dura of the middle cranial fossa
Dura of the posterior cranial fossa

questions.correctAnswerText: Dura of the anterior cranial fossa
questions.explanation: The dura of the anterior cranial fossa receives supply from all three divisions of the trigeminal nerve. The source lists anterior/posterior ethmoidal nerves from V1, nervus meningeus medius from V2, and nervus spinosus from V3.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The dura of the anterior cranial fossa receives supply from all three divisions of the trigeminal nerve. The source lists anterior/posterior ethmoidal nerves from V1, nervus meningeus medius from V2, and nervus spinosus from V3.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the nerve supply of the dura covering the marked region?

options.text: C2-C3 via cranial nerves X and XII

questions.correctAnswerText: C2-C3 via cranial nerves X and XII
questions.explanation: The dura of the posterior cranial fossa is mainly supplied by C2 and C3 fibers distributed via cranial nerves X and XII. Therefore C2-C3 via vagus and hypoglossal nerves is correct for the marked region.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The dura of the posterior cranial fossa is mainly supplied by C2 and C3 fibers distributed via cranial nerves X and XII. Therefore C2-C3 via vagus and hypoglossal nerves is correct for the marked region.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following arteries does not supply the corresponding region of the dura mater?

options.text: Middle meningeal artery — Anterior cranial fossa
Accessory meningeal branch of maxillary artery — Middle cranial fossa
Meningeal branch of internal carotid artery — Posterior cranial fossa
Meningeal branch of anterior and posterior ethmoid artery — Anterior cranial fossa

questions.correctAnswerText: Meningeal branch of internal carotid artery — Posterior cranial fossa
questions.explanation: The meningeal branch of the internal carotid artery does not supply the posterior cranial fossa; it contributes to anterior cranial fossa dura. The source lists ethmoidal/ICA branches for anterior fossa, middle/accessory meningeal and related branches for middle fossa, and occipital, vertebral and meningohypophyseal-derived branches for posterior fossa.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The meningeal branch of the internal carotid artery does not supply the posterior cranial fossa; it contributes to anterior cranial fossa dura. The source lists ethmoidal/ICA branches for anterior fossa, middle/accessory meningeal and related branches for middle fossa, and occipital, vertebral and meningohypophyseal-derived branches for posterior fossa.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is Meckel's cave formed by?

options.text: Evagination of the lower layer of the falx cerebri
Evagination of lower layer of the tentorium cerebelli

questions.correctAnswerText: Evagination of lower layer of the tentorium cerebelli
questions.explanation: Meckel's cave is an evagination of the lower layer of the tentorium cerebelli at the petrous apex. It is a dural recess in the middle cranial fossa that houses the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion and proximal trigeminal rootlets.
questions.structuredExplanationText: Meckel's cave is an evagination of the lower layer of the tentorium cerebelli at the petrous apex. It is a dural recess in the middle cranial fossa that houses the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion and proximal trigeminal rootlets.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with chronic otitis media and mastoiditis develops thrombosis of the sinus marked below. Which of the following sinuses does it drain from?
questions.explanation: The marked sinus is the sigmoid sinus, which continues from the transverse sinus. It follows an S-shaped groove near the mastoid, receives mastoid and condylar emissary veins, the venous plexus of the hypoglossal canal, inferior cerebellar veins and other tributaries, and joins the inferior petrosal sinus to form the internal jugular vein. Sigmoid/lateral sinus thrombosis can complicate ear or mastoid infection.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 54-year-old male came to the hospital with a severe headache. CT scan revealed an aneurysm of the internal carotid artery within the cavernous sinus. Which of the following nerves is likely to be affected first?

options.text: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
Maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve

questions.explanation: The abducens nerve is affected first because it runs within the cavernous sinus adjacent to the internal carotid artery. Oculomotor, trochlear and ophthalmic trigeminal fibers lie in the lateral wall and tend to be affected later. The maxillary division runs below the cavernous sinus rather than within it.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A diabetic lady with a history of chronic sinusitis presents with seizures and altered mental status. On examination, she is febrile and you note a left-sided lateral rectus palsy. On fundoscopy, papilledema is present bilaterally. Which of the following is not a tributary of the sinus involved here?
questions.explanation: The presentation suggests cavernous sinus thrombosis. The deep middle cerebral vein is not a tributary; it joins other deep cerebral veins to form the basal vein. Tributaries of the cavernous sinus include superior/inferior ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus, superficial middle cerebral vein and inferior cerebral vein. The source also lists drainage routes and contents including the cavernous ICA, sympathetic plexus, abducens nerve and lateral-wall cranial nerves.
